I always thought that I'd be able to "make it"; that some of the incredible ideas that I often have would come to fruition and I'd be able to move up and carve a life out for myself.

Instead, here I am. 27 years old, wasted years and money in university just drifting aimlessly. I "gave up" and took on a call centre job to buy myself time to "figure things out".

Instead of making any progress, I just stuck to the routine of working and running "errands" for my family. A whole year and then I got anxiety to the point where I would avoid going in to work (would sit in the car with panic attacks and drive off), so I ultimately ended up quitting. I was fairly good at what I did in the call centre, and was one of the youngest people promoted into the "supervisor" department. Spent lots of unpaid hours fixing things for clients, teaching the new guys tips and tricks, yet no one really cared when I left.

I don't even know why I'm writing here. I guess I've kind of just given up on life. It makes me really sad to say it, because I'm the "irrationally cheerful and happy" person that most people know-or at least used to know.

I've tried. I've really tried to get better. Saw a psychologist- her advice was to move out. Beyond that she wasn't very helpful (but was very expensive), so I stopped with that. I've tried getting out and meeting new people; I've tried dating, and each time it led to disappointment. I'm stuck in a family who would go apeshit if they knew I gave up on religion, who would do everything to prevent me from moving out. I've applied endlessly to jobs, with only Starbucks calling me back (I've managed stores, dispatched for the police, studied in science, I figured I'd be able to land something better than minimum wage).

I give up. I've let myself down, and I see really clearly that there isn't a happy- nor tolerable to a minimum type of future ahead.

Ok so here is my real advice. Stop comparing your progress to other people. I know it feels impossible but you have to stop because you are self sabotaging. This works for me when I am feeling overwhelmed: make a list of everything in your life that is upsetting you and seriously take the time on each one and figure out WHY it upsets you. For instance, 'Living at home" seems like it would be on your list and those feelings of inadequacy you have from it are cultural. In western culture 27 year old men aren't "supposed to" live at home, but that's not true everywhere. It's important to figure out what you feel and why you feel it and let yourself feel that feeling before you come up with a solution. That's one of the things I learned in my therapy. I'm the type of person that sees a problem and manically needs to fix that problem right away and that paralyzes me because I want to fix it without really looking at it. But make that list and really roll things over in your head and create steps to a solution. It's ok to ask for help with these steps. Is your family supportive?

There most likely is a happy ending here, but in this state of mind you wont be able to see it easily. You have to remember depression skews reality. That's very important.
